turns.en: And I think it touches on PMs need to be business leaders and great questions are often about the business and the future of the business and how to make it run more efficiently and this, and there's a product org element to it. But I find that that's a really underappreciated element of PM interviews, just thinking about the bigger business, not just the PM product.
turns.zh: 并且我认为这涉及到产品经理需要成为商业领袖，而好的面试问题通常会围绕业务、企业的未来发展，以及如何提升运营效率等展开——这其中也包含了产品组织层面的考量。但我发现，在产品经理面试中，这一环节往往被严重低估，人们往往只关注产品经理所负责的具体产品，而忽视了更宏观的商业视角。

turns.speaker: Jeremy Henrickson
turns.en: For me it's two things. It's thinking about the bigger business and having the context around whether it's revenue questions or strategy questions, but also the detailed questions. It's like, oh wait a minute. The implication of this thing that I'm getting asked or of this thing with Jeremy that you said earlier is all of these things. And their ability to understand that this isn't a simple business, it's really hard, it's really complex. And the ability to have these insights to help them think through those details is really cool.
turns.zh: 对我而言，关键有两点：一是从更宏观的商业视角出发，理解面试问题背后的深层含义——无论是关于营收的探讨，还是战略规划的探讨；二是关注细节。比如，当你被问到某个问题时，或者听到杰里米之前提到的某个案例时，要能联想到其背后隐藏的深层含义。产品经理需要理解商业环境的复杂性，认识到这份工作绝非易事，而是充满挑战。能够透过表象看清本质，帮助面试官理清思路的洞察力，实在令人赞赏。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You talked about this prompt you give product managers not to give away what you actually asked these days, but is there an example of a prompt that you've given in the past or you think is a good example of a type of prompt to give a product manager candidate.
turns.zh: 你提到现在不允许向产品经理透露具体面试问题，但能否举个过往的例子，或者分享一个你认为适合用来考察产品经理候选人的问题模板？

turns.speaker: Jeremy Henrickson
turns.en: In terms of a general kind of approach, I think a prompt should always reflect the actual business that they're going to kind of come into. So when we do, so our process overall is actually quite short. It's basically get in contact with us somehow, eventually get connected with a hiring manager, have a conversation with them. Then more or less you have a conversation with me, which is a product discussion. And then we have a case study which follows that. That's the whole process. Modulo, other conversations around the edges. And the questions that matter are around how do people think through that product discussion, which is relevant to our business. How do people think through that case study? That's number one. And the second thing is there's always a part of my interview, which is maybe sounds very simple, but it's just like, Hey, what questions do you have for me? (00:57:53): We actually do that before we do the product discussion. And that's an incredibly important question because it is again indicative of these things that people have thought through or not thought through or the depth that they're thinking or their interest in engagement in the role. And at that second discussion, it doesn't have to be perfect or anything, but it is a very strong signal when people, whether they've thought through a set of questions they want to ask or just on the fly generating them, you learn a lot about how people think about product, about what they're looking for, about what they like doing and not doing, just through those questions.
turns.zh: 就一般性的方法而言，我认为面试问题应该始终与应聘者将要从事的实际业务相关。因此，我们的整个流程实际上相当简短。首先，他们会以某种方式与我们取得联系，最终与招聘经理对话，然后与我进行产品讨论。接着是案例分析。除此之外，可能还会有一些其他交流环节。关键问题在于：应聘者如何思考产品讨论？这与我们的业务息息相关。如何看待案例分析？这才是首要问题。此外，在面试中我总会提出一个看似简单的问题——“你对我们有什么问题吗？”（00:57:53），我们通常在产品讨论前先进行这个环节。这是一个极其重要的环节，因为它能反映出应聘者是否深入思考过相关问题，或者他们对角色的兴趣程度。在第二次讨论中，问题不必完美无缺，但如果应聘者能提前构思好问题或即兴提问，这本身就是一个强烈的信号。通过这些问题，能深入了解应聘者对产品的理解、他们的求职动机、喜好与厌恶。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: For PMs that are maybe in their early career that are listening to this, what advice would you give them to help them accelerate and advance their career most in the early part of their career?
turns.zh: 对于那些处于职业生涯初期的产品经理，您会给他们什么建议，帮助他们在职业生涯早期加速成长并取得进步？

turns.speaker: Jeremy Henrickson
turns.en: Be humble. Being a product person means that by definition you're living in a world where no one knows the right answer yet because if somebody did, they would've already built it. And so having, no matter how smart you are, there's a lot of smart people out there. There's always stuff you don't know. There's always people who are going to know things that you don't know. And it is only through that acknowledgement that you can actually have the humility to say, I'm open to absorbing all of this stuff, I don't know. And open to synthesizing all this stuff and coming to different conclusions. (00:59:12): And so I found that that humility is one of the biggest differentiators in early career leaders who are able to let go of how awesome they were in school or in their first job or whatever. I mean, I had to do this and realize the job is always hard and the job is always about discovery every single day. And if you can maintain that curiosity and elasticity of thought and creativity and light coming solutions could be awesome. But if you close yourself off to that and think you always have the right answer, then there's like no hope.
turns.zh: 保持谦逊。作为产品从业者，注定要生活在一个尚未找到正确答案的世界里——因为如果有人找到了答案，他们早就把产品做出来了。无论你多么聪明，身边总有许多聪明的人。有太多东西是你不知道的，总有人知道你不知道的。只有承认这一点，你才能真正做到虚心求学、坦然承认自己的无知，并通过整合各种信息得出不同的结论。（00:59:12）。我发现，这种谦逊是早期职业生涯领导者的关键特质之一，他们能够放下在学校或第一份工作中建立的优越感。比如，我自己就经历过这个过程，意识到工作永远充满挑战，每天都需要不断探索。如果你能保持这种好奇心、思维的灵活性、创造力和开放心态，找到解决方案将非常棒。但如果你固执己见，认为自己永远正确，那就毫无希望了。
